q: A business buys office supplies for $300 cash. Which journal entry is correct?
r: Assets increase and another asset decreases.
w: Debit Supplies Expense $300; credit Owner's Capital $300
Capital is not affected by the purchase.

q: Which account type normally has a credit balance?
w: Drawing normally has a debit balance.

q: A trial balance shows total debits of $48,500 and total credits of $47,900. What does this indicate?
r: An error exists that must be found and corrected
w: A trial balance does not show profit.

q: What is the purpose of posting from the journal to the ledger?
r: To sort transaction amounts into individual accounts
The ledger shows each account's balance.

q: On December 31, a company has used $1,400 of prepaid insurance that was recorded as an asset. What adjusting entry is needed?
r: Debit Insurance Expense $1,400; credit Prepaid Insurance $1,400
The used portion becomes an expense.
w: Debit Prepaid Insurance $1,400; credit Insurance Expense $1,400

q: Which account is closed to Income Summary at the end of the period?
Revenues for the year are $82,000 and expenses are $61,500. What is the net income?
What is accrual-basis accounting?
r: Recording revenue when earned and expenses when incurred
Cash timing does not decide recognition.
w: Recording only when cash changes hands

q: A company earned $2,000 in service revenue in December but will not be paid until January. Under accrual accounting, when is the revenue recorded?
Which is the correct order of steps in the accounting cycle?
r: Journalize, post, trial balance, adjust, statements, close
Each step builds on the last.

q: What is a contra-asset account?
r: An account with a credit balance that reduces an asset
w: An account with a debit balance that increases an asset
An account that is always zero
An account used only for revenue

q: Equipment cost $12,000 with a $2,000 salvage value and a 5-year life. What is annual straight-line depreciation?
Why are adjusting entries needed?
r: To update accounts so revenues and expenses are recorded in the proper period

q: Wages of $900 have been earned by employees but will be paid next period. Which adjustment is needed?
r: Debit Wages Expense $900; credit Wages Payable $900
An accrued expense must be recorded.
w: No adjustment because no cash was paid

q: What does the post-closing trial balance contain?
r: Temporary accounts have been closed to zero.

q: What is a work sheet used for in accounting?
r: To organize trial balance and adjustments before preparing statements
It is an optional planning tool.

q: Total owner's equity at the start of the year was $50,000. Net income was $18,000 and the owner withdrew $6,000. What is ending equity?
A business sells $6,000 of goods on account with terms 2/10, n/30. What payment settles the invoice if paid on day 8?
Receivables total $80,000 and the company estimates 3% will be uncollectible. What is the bad debt estimate?
What does an aging schedule show?
r: How long receivables have been outstanding

q: What is the purpose of a purchase order?
r: To authorize a vendor to deliver goods or services at stated terms

q: A customer's $500 account is written off under the allowance method. What is the effect on net accounts receivable?
r: Both receivables and the allowance fall by $500.

q: What is a three-way match in accounts payable?
r: Comparing the purchase order, receiving report and invoice
It prevents paying for wrong or missing goods.

q: A company has $40,000 in credit sales and collects $32,000 during the period. What is the ending change in accounts receivable?
What is a credit memo from a seller?
r: A document reducing the amount a customer owes

q: Which statement shows revenues and expenses for a period?
w: That shows position at a date.

q: Assets total $120,000 and liabilities total $45,000. What is owner's equity?
On a classified balance sheet, which is a current asset?
r: It is expected to convert to cash within a year.

q: What does gross profit equal?
r: Net sales minus cost of goods sold
w: Net sales plus cost of goods sold
Cost of goods sold minus expenses

q: Net sales are $200,000 and gross profit is $80,000. What is the cost of goods sold?
What is the current ratio?
r: Current assets divided by current liabilities
w: Total assets divided by total sales

q: Current assets are $90,000 and current liabilities are $60,000. What is the current ratio?
Which statement explains changes in owner's equity during a period?
r: It shows capital, income and withdrawals.

q: What does the statement of cash flows divide activities into?
r: Each shows a source of cash.

q: Which is an example of a financing activity?
What does return on equity measure?
r: Net income relative to owners' investment

q: Net income is $30,000 and average equity is $200,000. What is return on equity?
A company has current assets of $55,000 and current liabilities of $38,000. What is its working capital?
What is the role of the FASB?
r: Setting accounting standards in the United States

q: A company records a sale before the goods ship and before the customer is obligated. Which principle is likely violated?
w: That concerns the size of items.

q: What is the going concern assumption?
r: A business will continue operating for the foreseeable future
w: A business will close next year
A business will never lose money

q: What is the purpose of an audit?
r: To give an independent opinion on whether financial statements are fairly presented

q: An auditor issues an unqualified opinion. What does this mean?
r: The statements are fairly presented in all material respects
w: The auditor refused to give an opinion

q: What does the Sarbanes-Oxley Act focus on?
r: Improving corporate financial reporting and internal controls
It was passed after major accounting scandals.

q: What is internal control?
r: Policies and procedures that protect assets and ensure accurate records

q: Which is an example of a strong internal control?
r: Requiring two signatures on checks over $5,000
w: Letting one clerk record and approve all payments

q: What does the cost principle say about recording assets?
r: Record assets at their original purchase cost
w: Record assets at the owner's estimate of value
Record assets at current market value only
That is not the cost principle.

q: A company wants to capitalize $50 for a stapler. Which concept allows expensing it immediately?
r: Small amounts need not be tracked as assets.
w: That is not the main concept.

q: What is conflict of interest in accounting?
r: A situation where personal interests may affect professional judgment
It must be disclosed or avoided.

q: An employee earns $1,000 gross. FICA is 7.65%. How much FICA tax is withheld?
w: That is ten times too high.

q: What does FICA fund?
What is Form 1099-NEC used for?
A business pays a freelance designer $3,500 in a year. Which form does it generally issue?
r: Payments of $600 or more are reported.

q: A taxpayer in the 22% bracket has a $1,000 deduction and a different taxpayer has a $1,000 credit. Who saves more?
r: The credit saves $1,000 and the deduction saves $220

q: What is a sales tax permit used for?
r: Allowing a seller to collect and report sales tax

q: What is a payroll tax liability?
r: Taxes withheld or owed on wages that must be paid to the government
They remain a liability until remitted.

q: A business collects $2,400 in sales tax during the month. Until it pays the state, how should this be recorded?
r: As Sales Tax Payable, a liability
w: It is not the company's income.

q: What is cloud accounting software?
r: Accounting programs accessed online instead of on one computer
Data can be reached from many devices.

q: What is a key control risk of cloud-based accounting?
r: Unauthorized access if passwords or permissions are weak
w: Data can never be backed up

q: What does an electronic spreadsheet do well in accounting?
r: Perform calculations and organize data automatically

q: What is optical character recognition used for in accounting?
r: Reading printed documents and turning them into digital data

q: A company automates invoice approval with software. What is a likely benefit?
r: Faster processing and fewer manual errors

q: Why should accounting data be backed up regularly?
r: To recover records if data is lost or damaged
w: To make data harder to read

q: What is blockchain's possible use in accounting?
r: A secure shared ledger of transactions

q: What does a certified public accountant (CPA) do?
r: Provides accounting, audit and tax services after meeting licensing requirements
The license requires exams and experience.

q: A student enjoys finding errors and checking details. Which accounting career might fit best?
What does a bookkeeper typically do?
What is a forensic accountant?
r: A specialist who investigates financial fraud and disputes

q: Which skill is most important for a staff accountant?
What does a management accountant do?
r: Prepares information to help managers make decisions
Budgets and cost analysis are common.

q: What is the accounting equation?
A business pays $2,000 of its accounts payable with cash. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
r: Assets and liabilities both decrease by $2,000

q: What does double-entry bookkeeping mean?
r: Every transaction affects at least two accounts
w: Every transaction is recorded twice in the same account
Two people must sign every entry

q: Which is an example of a liability?
An owner invests $15,000 cash in a new business. How is the transaction recorded?
What is a source document?
r: A record that proves a transaction occurred

q: What is the business entity concept?
r: A business's records are kept separate from its owner's personal records
w: The owner and business are always the same
Records are kept only for customers

q: An owner pays a personal electric bill from the business checking account. How should it be recorded?
r: As owner's drawing, not a business expense
w: As utilities expense of the business
It is not a business cost.

q: What is the normal balance of the owner's drawing account?
w: That is for revenue and equity.

q: What is a chart of accounts?
r: A list of all accounts a business uses, with account numbers

q: Which account number range typically represents assets in a chart of accounts?
